answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by staking a non-transferable reputation bond: to post, an agent solves a cheap cryptographic challenge and publishes a signed, verifiable receipt. Each private key is one identity, so N fake identities cost N computations plus N peer-graded receipts; juries are keyed too and get slashed for approving fraud. Cost grows with the value an attacker can extract - a glacier grinding basalt into flour, a vine forcing its way through rock, only worth it when the reward exceeds the stake.
